rubric: Analyst-assigned 0-10 axes. I=impact, E=exploitability, R=reachability, D=detectability. Weights and tiers live in config/research.yaml.

CVE-2026-105659.notes: Timer-reset trickle attack; needs sustained low-rate WINDOW_UPDATEs, good for a long-duration lab run rather than a quick PoC.

CVE-2026-105660.notes: Trivial to send a crafted request-target; real impact depends entirely on whether the app trusts conn.host/conn.port for authz or routing decisions.

CVE-2026-108525.notes: Requires understanding Bandit's flow-control accounting (send WINDOW_UPDATE generously, never let the stream process drain) -- more h2 state-machine work than 116078.

CVE-2026-108529.notes: Quadratic cost needs many blocked streams plus repeated SETTINGS/stream-0 WINDOW_UPDATE; more streams to orchestrate.

CVE-2026-109584.notes: Cookie-crumb join amplification depends on HPACK header-block construction, more encoding nuance than raw frame spam.

CVE-2026-110314.notes: Post-close frame delivery; mostly an application-correctness/isolation issue, modest direct security impact.

CVE-2026-110499.notes: HPACK dynamic-table size update per response; needs many requests over one connection to accumulate state.

CVE-2026-111101.notes: Plain HTTP/1.1, no TLS/ALPN juggling, no auth, no special client lib. Single connection, trickle 1-byte chunks. Easiest PoC in the set.

CVE-2026-111103.notes: Requires driving streams into StreamError recovery repeatedly to roll back connection-level counters; more protocol-edge-case orchestration.

CVE-2026-113436.notes: Oversized Content-Length / Host port digit strings; trivial to construct, impact is parse-time CPU not memory.

CVE-2026-114213.notes: 1-byte continuation frames bypassing max_fragmented_message_size; needs a WS handshake first but payload construction is simple.

CVE-2026-114216.notes: Needs a front-end proxy with different line-ending tolerance in front of Bandit to matter; pure-Bandit repro shows parser behavior only, not smuggling impact.

CVE-2026-115269.notes: Same family as 105659 -- SETTINGS/WINDOW_UPDATE resets the body-read timeout instead of the blocked-send deadline.

CVE-2026-116078.notes: Needs an HTTP/2 client (h2) but otherwise a single stream of 1-byte DATA frames; very clean memory signal, good PoC candidate.

CVE-2026-39803.notes: Body-size cap silently not enforced during streaming reads; needs a body-consuming Plug but no other prerequisite.

CVE-2026-39804.notes: permessage-deflate zip-bomb; requires negotiating the extension and crafting a compressible payload -- moderately more work.

CVE-2026-39805.notes: CL.CL duplicate Content-Length; same caveat -- exploitability is a property of the proxy/Bandit pair, not Bandit alone.

CVE-2026-39806.notes: Needs a trailer-bearing chunked request to hit the decoder loop; slightly more wire-format precision than the two above.

CVE-2026-39807.notes: Client-supplied scheme trusted without transport check; impact is app-level (e.g. incorrect redirect/secure-cookie logic) not Bandit crashing.

CVE-2026-42786.notes: Unbounded fragment reassembly pre-1.11; same shape as 114213 on an older code path.

CVE-2026-42788.notes: Frame-size check ordering bug; impact capped at VA:L per CVSS, smaller blast radius than the rest of the HTTP/2 family.

CVE-2026-65623.notes: Quadratic CPU on fragment reassembly; CPU-bound rather than memory-bound, needs wall-clock timing to observe cleanly.

CVE-2026-74836.notes: Connection-window starvation pins Plug processes; needs the connection window, not just stream windows, held at zero.

CVE-2026-75484.notes: CRLF/NUL in HTTP/2 header values reaching the app; impact is header/log/response-splitting downstream of Bandit, not in Bandit itself.
